scenario: WIBTA for kicking my girlfriends older sister out of our apartment? | Apologies in advance. This is a really long story. I’ve lived with my girlfriend for 2 years. We moved to the apartment we are at now a year ago. We used to live with her sister and another couple. We’ll call my girlfriend L and her sister J. We moved because J would always have people over , and we wanted the privacy of no roommates. Once we moved, someone took our spot there. Fast forward from when we left (May 2018) to January 1st, 2020. J fucked her roommates over by not paying the rent for two months, as our landlords just accepted cash. For two months, she took the $3000 spent it on “bills” that her sister isn’t even sure about. After ruining her relationship with her roommates, She got the money from family to pay the rent off, and asked L and I to move in until the end of January. Her uncle would pick her up and she’d move out of state. She basically never asked the uncle to come get her, mentioned to L that she might just stay in New York. My girlfriend, who isn’t confrontational, never opposed her living with us for free. So J has been with us for about 4 months, no job, just contributing sometimes with cooking. She only comes here to sleep after she parties with her friends. Our house is essentially a hangover den. What makes matters worse is because of the current situation, the job she had a chance at has shut down. So shes not even looking for work. But that isn’t stopping her from going out every other night, to parties, where she doesn’t even think that if she was to get sick from being stupid, it would affect us as well. L wants her out, but is really conflicted because it’s her sister. I don’t think she’d be happy about me speaking to J about it, even though she also wants J out. I don’t want to seem like a dick, but it’s at the point where I might just take the risk of L being mad at me. I want my home back. I’ve been trying to get L to talk to her, but she just hates confrontation. I think I might just have to tell J if she doesn’t find a job to fund her getting her own place, she needs to to back to her mothers. WIBTA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to kick my girlfriend's older sister out of our apartment. Let me start by laying out the situation as I understand it. We've been living together for two years, and we moved to our current apartment a year ago. The main reason we moved was because her sister, J, was always having people over, and we wanted more privacy without roommates. That worked out well until recently when J ended up moving back in with us. From what I gather, J had some issues with her previous roommates. She didn't pay rent for two months, which caused some financial strain. The landlords were accepting cash, so it's unclear if they were aware of the situation. J then got money from her family to pay off the rent and asked my girlfriend, L, and me to let her stay with us until the end of January. However, it seems like J didn't make proper arrangements for her uncle to pick her up, and she mentioned possibly staying in New York instead. L, my girlfriend, isn't confrontational, so she didn't oppose J moving in for free. Now, J has been staying with us for about four months without a job. She sometimes helps with cooking, but that's inconsistent. She parties with her friends every other night, comes home to sleep, and our place has become a hangover den. Because of the current situation, the job J had a chance at has shut down, so she's not even looking for work. Despite this, she continues to go out partying, which is concerning because if she were to get sick from being reckless, it could affect all of us. I want J out because our home is becoming chaotic, and I want our privacy back. I'm conflicted because it's her sister, and I don't want to upset L by speaking to J about it, even though L also wants J out. I don't want to seem like a jerk, but things have gotten to the point where I might have to take the risk of L being mad at me. I've tried getting L to talk to her, but she hates confrontation. I'm considering telling J that if she doesn't find a job to fund her own place, she needs to go back to her mother's. So, is it right or wrong for me to kick her out? I need to think about the dynamics here. On one hand, J is taking advantage of our hospitality without contributing financially or emotionally. She's causing a disturbance in our home, which we moved to for privacy. On the other hand, she's family, and L might be hesitant to confront her. I should consider the impact on L. If I take action, L might be upset with me, but she also wants J out. Maybe she's just avoiding the confrontation. I should also think about J's situation. She's in a tough spot financially and might not have many options. However, she's not making any effort to improve her situation, which is frustrating. Another angle is the fairness of asking J to leave. We have a right to our own space and privacy. J's behavior is affecting our living conditions, and it's reasonable to want her to leave. However, since she's family, there might be an expectation to help her out, but that doesn't mean we have to sacrifice our own well-being. I also need to think about the practical steps. If I decide to ask J to leave, how will that conversation go? How will L react? Maybe I should approach it gently, explaining how her presence is affecting our home and that we need some space. It's possible that J might not take it well, but it's necessary for our peace of mind. In the end, I believe that while it's difficult, it's the right thing to do to ask J to leave. Our home should be a sanctuary for us, and J's behavior is making it anything but. It's important to stand up for our needs, even if it means confronting family members. L might be upset initially, but she also wants J out, so she might understand in the long run.
